items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Arstella had presented herself to me after a concert... told me that she knew a little girl in Rochester whom I called my niece... landed a contract for Arstella, Fred Palmer and myself to appear as an attraction in a cabaret called Florida Club

ctx.x: In Geneva with Jack Dieval was Kenny Clarke on drums, Paul Vernon a French tenor man, Emmanuel Soudieux, also French, on bass, and an American Negro singer, named Arstella Whitter from Rochester, N.Y.

Arstella had presented herself to me after a concert at the Edouard 7th theatre, my first or second one, and told me that she knew a little girl in Rochester whom I called my niece but she actually was not related to me. I never knew how Arstella happened to come across to France,and as a singer. I had never heard of her in the States, but she had a nice voice in the style of Ella Fitzgerald, when she sang sweet numbers.

Paul Vernon I had met soon after I came to Paris. He played tenor in the style of Dexter Gordon whom he admired with a little mixture of Prez(Lester Young). As for Jack Dieval, he was a good business man who probably had classical training on the piano and came into the jazz field because he liked that type of music and especially the blues.
